purpose: Where does the stage finish after a whole number of repeated corrections?
meaning: A geometric series adds terms with one common ratio. A partial sum adds a finite whole number of terms. Its closed form has a separate r=1 case. With a nonzero first term, the infinite geometric series has a finite sum exactly when the ratio has magnitude less than one.

definition.setting: A positioning script sends a first forward correction a centimetres. Each later signed correction is r times the previous correction. Add exactly n commands to find the endpoint. A negative ratio alternates forward and backward corrections; the signed sum is net displacement, not distance travelled or a simulation of a mechanical controller.

signature.k: Bound summation index, from zero through n minus one
signature.∞: Unbounded summation limit, not a finite term count

conditions: The first correction a lies in [0.25,4] cm, ratio r in [−1.5,1.5], and n is a whole number from 1 through 12. Every finite sum is defined, including r=1. Because a is nonzero, the infinite series has a finite sum only for |r|<1. Integer commands do not interpolate into fractional terms. Numeric sums use a compensated recurrence; nonzero term underflow is reported explicitly.

properties.claim: Finite partial sums remain defined when no infinite-series sum exists.
properties.conditions: The first correction a lies in [0.25,4] cm, ratio r in [−1.5,1.5], and n is a whole number from 1 through 12. Every finite sum is defined, including r=1. Because a is nonzero, the infinite series has a finite sum only for |r|<1. Integer commands do not interpolate into fractional terms. properties.derivation: Subtract r times a finite sum from that sum to obtain (1−r)Sₙ=a(1−rⁿ). When r=1, add n equal terms. For |r|<1 the power tends to zero; for |r|≥1 with nonzero a the terms do not tend to zero.
